text: Write a program that reveals what a `double` actually holds when you write 0.1. Fill in the two blanks.
choices: System.out.println(___);   // the exact stored value of the double 0.1
System.out.println(___);   // the shortest decimal that round-trips
explanation: Verified: the first prints 0.1000000000000000055511151231257827021181583404541015625 and the second prints 0.1. The contrast is the lesson. `new BigDecimal(double)` shows the binary fraction exactly; `BigDecimal.valueOf(double)` goes through the shortest decimal that maps back to the same double, which is what `toString` prints. So the 0.1 you see is a display convention, and the value underneath has never been one tenth.
